definitions.explanation: A person who buys and sells goods for profit.

examples.japanese: {商人|しょうにん}が{店|みせ}を{開|ひら}いた。
{大阪|おおさか}は{昔|むかし}から{商人|しょうにん}の{町|まち}として{知|し}られている。
examples.english: Osaka has long been known as a city of merchants.

examples.japanese: その{商人|しょうにん}は{外国|がいこく}との{貿易|ぼうえき}で{財|ざい}を{成|な}した。
examples.english: That merchant made a fortune through foreign trade.

examples.japanese: {江戸時代|えどじだい}の{商人|しょうにん}は{社会的|しゃかいてき}な{地位|ちい}が{低|ひく}かった。
examples.english: Merchants had low social status during the Edo period.
examples.notes: Historically, merchants (商人) were at the bottom of the four-class system (士農工商)

examples.japanese: {町|まち}の{商人|しょうにん}たちは{朝|あさ}{早|はや}くから{店|みせ}を{開|あ}け、{夜|よる}{遅|おそ}くまで{働|はたら}いて{家族|かぞく}を{支|ささ}えていた。
examples.english: The merchants in town would open their shops early in the morning and work until late at night to support their families.

notes:
{商人|しょうにん} is a somewhat formal or literary word for a merchant or trader. In modern usage, it often appears in historical contexts or when referring to traditional business people.

RELATED TERMS:
- {商売人|しょうばいにん}: businessperson, tradesman (everyday tone)
- {商店|しょうてん}{主|しゅ}: shop owner
- {貿易|ぼうえき}{商|しょう}: trading company/trader

HISTORICAL NOTE:
In the Edo period class system ({士農工商|しのうこうしょう}: samurai, farmers, artisans, merchants), merchants were officially ranked lowest, yet many became extremely wealthy.

CULTURAL NOTE:
{大阪|おおさか} has long been known as a city of merchants ({商人|しょうにん}の{町|まち}), and the expression {大阪商人|おおさかしょうにん} refers to the shrewd, business-savvy character associated with the city.
